line: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be2 e6
teaches: Some moves are a choice of MOVE and some are a choice of STRUCTURE — pick knowingly, because everything you do for the next twenty moves follows from it. To the sixth rank keeps the centre flexible and the light squares guarded; a square further seizes space and concedes one square for good.
explains: Some moves choose a move; this one chooses a structure. Push the pawn two squares and you grab space but hand over a square for good — play it to e6 instead and the centre stays fluid, nothing conceded. On e6 it covers d5 and f5, the two squares a knight would kill to reach in front of this structure. Pick it knowingly: everything for the next twenty moves flows from here.
